accesses.location: Access by portage only in BWCA on USFS land.

surveys.narrative:
Temperature and dissolved oxygen measurements were collected in the deepest basin in Bear Trap Lake, on July 31, 2024, to evaluate the quantity and quality of cold, oxygenated water (i.e., oxythermal habitat) available to Cisco, also known as Tullibee, the most sensitive coldwater species present in this lake. During the summer, Cisco require a layer of oxythermal habitat that contains water temperatures below 21.2 degrees C (70.2 degrees F) and dissolved oxygen concentrations above 3.0 mg/L. Based on the profile from the deepest basin, the water temperature decreased to below 21.2 degrees C (70.2 degrees F) at 8.1 feet and the dissolved oxygen concentration decreased to 3.0 mg/L at 8.4 feet at the time of sampling. The thickness of this layer of water in the water column was 0.36 feet, indicating that very limited oxythermal habitat was present for Cisco.

Further, the temperature at which dissolved oxygen decreased to 3.0 mg/L (i.e., TDO3, a single variable to characterize oxythermal habitat) was 20.6 degrees C (69.1 degrees F). TDO3 values cooler than 21.2 degrees C (70.2 degrees F) indicate that oxythermal conditions were suitable for Cisco, however the layer of suitable habitat was confined to well less than 3 feet for Cisco at the time of the survey.

This is the first survey completed on Bear Trap Lake during the late summer period of maximum oxythermal stress. When inadequate oxythermal habitat is available, Cisco are squeezed into unfavorable, warmer water conditions and experience higher levels of stress.

The present fish population consists of an average size sucker population and northern pike population. The northern pike population seems to have many missing younger age classes, indicating low reproduction. The walleye population is well above average with most year classes represented.

Temperature and dissolved oxygen (DO) measurements were collected from the deepest basin in Bear Trap Lake on August 2nd, 2025, to evaluate the quantity and quality of cold, oxygenated water (i.e., oxythermal habitat) available to Cisco, also known as Tullibee, the most sensitive coldwater species present in this lake. During the summer, Cisco require a layer of oxythermal habitat that contains water temperatures below 21.2 degrees C (70.2 degrees F) and dissolved oxygen concentrations above 3.0 mg/L. Based on the profile from the deepest basin (maximum sampled depth 34.4 feet), the water temperature decreased below 21.2 degrees C (70.2 degrees F) at 9.0 feet and the dissolved oxygen concentration decreased to 3.0 mg/L at 13.5 feet at the time of sampling. The thickness of this layer of water in the water column was 4.5 feet, indicating that oxythermal habitat was present for Cisco.

Further, the temperature at which dissolved oxygen decreased to 3.0 mg/L (i.e., TDO3, a single variable to characterize oxythermal habitat) was 15.0 degrees C (59.0 degrees F). TDO3 values cooler than 21.2 degrees C (70.2 degrees F) indicate that oxythermal conditions were suitable for Cisco at the time of the survey.

Data collected by the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources during the late summer period of maximum oxythermal stress (July 26th to Aug 24th) in 2024 also indicates suitable oxythermal habitat. The least favorable conditions were recorded in 2024 when the suitable oxythermal habitat layer was 0.4 feet thick. When inadequate oxythermal habitat is available, Cisco are squeezed into unfavorable, warmer water conditions and experience higher levels of stress.
